gap: No result ChatGPT got states which exact extra batteries and adapters each 3,000 W station takes: EcoFlow's US store lists three packs and a $199 two-battery adapter for the DELTA 3 Max Plus, DJI allows ten Expansion Battery 2000 units on the Power 2000, and BLUETTI's Apex 200 reaches 3,600 W only with an expansion battery or AC/solar input.
standout_why: Compared against rvgearlab.com (best-3000-watt page, updated 2026-10-02), powerstationsrated.com, wattsift.com, truewattlab.com, powerstations.reviews/jackery-3000 and Anker's F3000 page. RV Gear Lab gives 'Expands from 2kWh to 10kWh with extra batteries' for the DELTA 3 Max Plus and names no pack. WattSift gives expansion totals only and says of the F3000 '240 V output is not confirmed'. Power Stations Rated and TrueWattLab carry no accessory pairings. powerstations.reviews already states the HomePower 3000 takes no extra batteries, and Anker's own page already states the F3000 cells, so those are not new. Caveat: I could not read the cited EcoFlow manual PDF (it came back as binary and the text-extraction command was not permitted), so it may already name the compatible packs; the $199 adapter and its cross-model list are less likely to be in it.
decides: It confirms rather than overturns the pick. The DELTA 3 Max Plus ($1,149 at EcoFlow US, available) answers its 2,048 Wh runtime weakness with three named add-on packs, while the HomePower 3000 cannot grow, per powerstations.reviews. The F3000 is 120 V only alone, and Anker's page shows it sold out with orders shipping in 3–7 weeks. Our BLUETTI Apex 200 meets the 3,000 W line on its own at 3,200 W, but its 3,600 W figure is conditional and orders placed on or after Nov 25 ship from mid-February, which is beyond the four-week rule for a pick. The DJI Power 2000 gets solar only through a separately named adapter or charger, and DJI's spec page names no 30 A RV outlet.
